      Remove Workit from the picked or named hosts (keeps the Workit config)
  workit grant [show|set|unset] [options]

  workit approve <id>…
      Ask the user to approve a Workit request; their yes is recorded once
  workit config show [options]
      Show the effective config here and where each value comes from
  workit workspace [list|add|set|rm] [options]
      Edit workspace entries without the wizard; a raise (rm included) needs the user at a terminal

  workit <family> <action> [options]

  workit check <name> [--full] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--wait <dur> | --no-wait] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] | workit check [--name <n>] [--shell] [--full] [--timeout <s>] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--heavy [--wait <dur> | --no-wait]] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] -- <cmd…>
      Run a configured or ad-hoc check and record CLI-observed evidence (exit = the command's); heavy checks wait for the machine-wide heavy-check lease
  workit lock status|reap|cancel|wait|run|heavy [options]
      The machine-wide heavy-check lease: who holds it, wait for it, run a command under it, and which shell commands count as heavy
  workit models show [options]

  workit pr status|create|template|ready|edit|threads|reply|merge [options]

  workit issue view|comment|close|create [options]

  workit ci wait|rerun|logs [options]
      Wait for CI on the PR head (exit 0/1/3/4), read the failing jobs' log tails, or rerun failed jobs once per head
  workit git branch|commit|stage|unstage|push|rebase|hold|trailers [options]
      Policy-checked branch, hunk staging and commit (Workit-Session trailer); push with a lease and the tip verified
  workit release start|finish|publish|notes [options]
      git-flow releases without the git-flow binary: start a local release branch, finish it (merge, tag, merge back, push, forge release), publish it only when asked
  workit verify-delivery [push|pr|merge|release] [options]
      Observe that a push, PR head, merge or release really landed on the remote (exit 1 when not)

      Plan, restack (lease push + retarget) and land a base-branch stack of PRs, root first

  workit ledger decision|ruling|verdict|list|check|verify-integrity|void|standing|add [options]
      Record and query decisions, rulings, SHA-keyed verdicts (patch-id carry across rebases) and a fanout's standing orders
  workit test-audit [paths…] [--diff [<base>]] [--rule <ids>] [--min-severity <level>] [--fail-on <level>] [--mutate [--test-cmd <cmd {files}>] [--max-mutants <n>] [--budget <s>] [--timeout <s>]]
      Flag tautological and low-value tests with a suggested independent oracle; --mutate checks changed lines with diff-scoped mutation
  workit deslop scan|result [options]
      Classify the comments, suppressions and debug leftovers a branch adds, by review lane, with no agent
  workit knowledge lint [options]
      Lint agent knowledge files: AGENTS.md byte budget, broken local links, scaffold-only files, duplicated rules (exit 1 on findings)
  workit youtrack note|time|meeting|show|create [options]
      YouTrack issues and time; writes ask first unless youtrack.writes: auto
  workit changelog apply|merge|driver [options]
      Add entries under the Unreleased section of the changelog
  workit handoff [--note <t>] [--next <t>] [--record] [--last <n>] | workit handoff --task <id>
      Print a resume brief (branch, HEAD, dirty state, verdict, rulings, next command); --task exports v1 task state

Global flags:
  --json             Machine-readable output: {"ok","code","data","error"?,"unblock"?}
  --cwd <dir>        Run as if started in <dir>
  --session <id>     Act as session <id> (before the command; same as WORKIT_SESSION_ID=<id>, which it beats)
  --version          Print the CLI version
  -h, --help         Show usage for the command and subcommand before it (runs nothing)

part.text: The contract for this verb is explicit: only the user runs `--yes` or the picker, in their own terminal; an agent may run `--preview`. So let me produce the preview for Cursor only.

part.text:
I did not remove anything — this verb is gated to the user's own terminal, and I'll respect that rather than route around it.

**What a Cursor-only uninstall would do** (from `workit uninstall --hosts=cursor --preview`, nothing changed):

| Action | Target |
|---|---|
| Edit JSON | `~/.cursor/settings.json` — remove `enabled_plugins.workit` |
| Edit JSON | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` — remove `mcpServers.workit` |
| Remove dir | `~/.cursor/plugins/local/workit` |

Your Workit config in `<world>/config` is always kept, and the preview lists no paths outside `.cursor` — so claude-code, codex, opencode and pi would be left alone, as you asked.

**Run this yourself in a terminal:**

```
workit uninstall --hosts=cursor --yes
```

Two notes so the result isn't a surprise:

- `--hosts=cursor` skips the interactive picker entirely, so you won't be asked about the owned CLI install. Cursor was likely not the host that installed the Workit binary; if you also want the CLI gone, that's a separate decision (`workit upgrade` / `doctor` won't do it — check `workit hel p` output for the CLI handling in the picker, or just run the picker without `--hosts` and deselect everything but the CLI question).
- Since the uninstall edits JSON in place, Cursor should be closed while it runs. If the `settings.json` edit fails, that's the usual cause.

If you'd rather I verify the post-state, run the command and I'll confirm the three targets are gone and the other hosts' configs are unchanged.
